newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel lowers duties on processed-food imports.
newsitem.headline: Israel lowers duties on processed-food imports.

text.p: The Israeli ministerial economics committee on Monday lowered duties on processed-food imports by 12 to 50 percentage points effective immediately, the Treasury said.
Under a phased-in programme, duties on processed foods were to fall on January 1 but the committee did not give approval until Monday.

Israel removed administrative barriers on processed-food imports from January 1, 1996 to meet World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules. In addition, Israel undertook unilaterally to lower customs rates over a seven-year period.
The liberalisation covers all processed foods except bakery goods, coffee and chocolates. It is aimed at bringing the base customs rate down to eight percent by the year 2002.
